technical_and_design_decisions: Use Docker's native linking and environment variable mechanisms for external service configuration (U1).
Adopt Spring Cloud Service Discovery (e.g., Consul or Eureka) for service discovery in Docker XD containers (U2).
Implement CI/CD pipeline using Jenkins (or GitLab CI) to build, test, and deploy Docker images to a registry (U3).
Documentation for Mesos/Marathon deployment will be written in Markdown and integrated into the project's documentation site (U4).
Upgrade Spring Boot from 2.7.x to 3.0.x (aligned with Spring Framework 6.0 and Java 17+) and address breaking changes (U5).
Introduce a partitioning strategy interface for the JDBC source module, allowing configuration via job DSL or servers.yml (U6).
Develop a new HDFS source module supporting multiple file formats (text, Avro, Parquet) and integrate with XD's module deployment (U7).
Add a global 'commit-interval' property in servers.yml and modify all out-of-the-box partitioned jobs to read this property (U8).
All new configuration properties will follow Spring Boot's externalized configuration conventions.
Integration tests will use Testcontainers for Docker, embedded Hadoop/HDFS, and a local Mesos/Marathon cluster where feasible.
assumptions: The codebase is a maintained fork of Spring XD (or Spring Cloud Data Flow) compatible with Spring Framework 6.0 and Java 17+.
The development team has expertise in Spring, Docker, Hadoop/HDFS, Mesos/Marathon, and CI/CD tools.
A CI server (Jenkins/GitLab) and Docker registry are already available and only need pipeline configuration.
Existing modules for JDBC source and HDFS sink are present and can be extended.
The 'servers.yml' configuration file is the central configuration for XD server runtime properties.
Service discovery implementation will leverage Spring Cloud Commons abstractions to remain backend-agnostic.
Documentation for U4 is standalone and does not require code changes.
Spring Boot upgrade (U5) is limited to the Spring XD runtime and its modules, not the entire Spring ecosystem.
All development work is performed by a single developer (no parallel work), so estimates are sequential.
Testing includes unit, integration, and manual verification; no separate QA team.

activities.activity_name: Service Discovery Integration for Docker XD Containers
activities.activity_description: Evaluate, select, and integrate a service discovery mechanism (e.g., Consul, Eureka) with Spring Cloud. Implement service registration and discovery for XD processes in a clustered Docker environment. Includes configuration, health checks, and cluster testing.

activities.activity_name: CI Build Pipeline for Docker Images
activities.activity_description: Set up a CI/CD pipeline (Jenkins/GitLab CI) to build Docker images for all XD components, run automated tests (unit, integration), and deploy images to a Docker registry with promotion across environments (dev, staging, prod).
